Plants have evolved defenses almost as diverse as the number of genera. Some load their tissues with harsh compounds that either are unpleasant to insects or intoxicate them, __(A) encouraging__ the insects to go bother another plant or at least slowing down their eating. Structural defenses like thick coats of wax on leaves may prevent some insect species from __(B) damaging__ the plant tissues altogether. Nor are individual plants entirely on their own while under attack. Plants can release chemical compounds that let their same-species neighbors __(C) known__ that an attack is likely coming, pushing those nearby plants to start building up defensive compounds in their tissues. Some of these cues even attract insect predators, a call for an assist that benefits both the plant and its bug-eating collaborators. The back-and-forth is not a matter of natural balance, but more like a drawn-out evolutionary conversation. New plant defenses unintentionally select for insects with ways to get around them, __(D) which__ in turn help bring about more resilient and resistant plant species. New variations, shading into entire new forms and adaptations, __(E) maintain__ the stalemate.

question.questionText:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Kant staunchly advocated for the rule of law as the fundamental assurance, providing not just for security and peace, but for liberty as well.. He believed that human societies were moving towards more rational forms regulated by effective and binding legal frameworks because only such frameworks enabled people to live in harmony, to prosper and to co-operate. However, his belief in inevitable progress was not based on an optimistic or high-minded view of human nature. On the contrary, it comes close to Hobbes's outlook: man's violent and conflict-prone nature makes it necessary to establish and maintain an effective legal framework in order to secure peace. We cannot count on people's benevolence or goodwill, but even 'a nation of devils' can live in harmony in a legal system that binds every citizen equally. Ideally, the law is the embodiment of those political principles that all rational beings would freely choose. If such laws forbid them to do something that they would not rationally choose to do anyway, then the law _____.

options.text: serves to strip away the basic conditions for co-operative living
options.label: ①

options.text: is far from being a genuine reflection of their rational choices
options.label: ②

options.text: does not actually function as a limitation on their liberty
options.label: ③

options.text: should be seen as a necessary evil to keep their desires in check
options.label: ④

options.text: inevitably fails to protect them from external physical threats
options.label: ⑤

structuredData.direction: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
keyPoints: 칸트의 법치주의 관점에서 법의 지배와 개인의 자유가 상충하지 않고 공존하는 인과적 기제를 파악합니다.
이성적 주체가 동의할 수 있는 규범으로서의 법이 왜 제한(restraint)이 될 수 없는지 담화 맥락을 연결합니다.
liberty와 freedom, restraint와 limitation 등의 유의어 쌍을 활용한 고급 추상 재진술을 읽어냅니다.
structuredData.answerLogic: 합리적인 사회적 구성원이 스스로 선택했을 도덕적·정치적 원칙이 곧 법으로 재현된 것이라면, 그러한 법적 금지는 개인의 순수한 자유의지를 침해하는 억압이 아니라 자율적 합의의 확장이라는 논리적 상관관계를 완성하는 추론입니다.
structuredData.explanation: 빈칸 문장은 이성적 존재가 자유롭게 선택했을 정치적 원칙의 구현체로서의 '법'이 가진 성격과 그것이 개인의 자유와 맺는 인과적 귀결을 맺어 주는 결론적 지점입니다. 지문 초반부에서 칸트는 법의 지배가 안전과 평화뿐만 아니라 '자유(liberty)' 역시 보장한다고 천명하였으며, 지문 끝에서 이성적인 법이 애초에 우리가 자발적으로 하지 않을 행동을 금지할 뿐이라면 그것은 간섭이 아니라고 설명합니다. 따라서 그러한 법적 규제는 실질적으로 우리의 자유를 제한하는 장치로 기능하지 않는다는 추론이 성립하므로, 원문의 'cannot be understood as a restraint on their freedom'을 'does not actually function as a limitation on their liberty'로 자율적이고 추상화하여 패러프레이즈한 ③이 정답입니다. ④과 ①는 법을 온전히 억압적이고 파괴적인 기제로 파악하는 극성 반전의 함정을 파고들며, ②는 이성적 선택과의 연결을 부정하는 역관계의 오류입니다.

The basic guidelines for good style __(A) are__ not mysterious; in fact, you use them every day in conversation. In conversation and in writing, we all rely heavily on cooperation to make sense of exchanges, and a polished practical style makes cooperation easier. Writers develop such a style by acknowledging __(B) those__ readers expect the same things that listeners expect in conversation: clarity, relevance, and proportion. If you listen to someone __(C) who__ is not clear, who cannot stay on the topic, or who offers too much or too little information, you will quickly lose interest in the conversation. Writers, too, need to be clear, stay on the topic, and give information appropriately. In fact, this attention to audience and appropriateness may be even __(D) more important__ in writing than in conversation because writing does not permit the nonverbal communication and immediate feedback __(E) that__ are part of conversation. As writers, we have to anticipate the absent reader's response; in effect, we have to imagine both halves of a virtual conversation.

Plants have evolved defenses almost as diverse as the number of genera. Some load their tissues with harsh compounds that either are unpleasant to insects or intoxicate them, encouraging the insects to go bother another plant or at least slowing down their eating. Structural defenses like thick coats of wax on leaves may prevent some insect species from damaging the plant tissues altogether. Nor are individual plants entirely on their own while under attack. Plants can release chemical compounds that let their same-species neighbors know that an attack is likely coming, pushing those nearby plants to start building up defensive compounds in their tissues. Some of these cues even attract insect predators, a call for an assist that benefits both the plant and its bug-eating collaborators. The back-and-forth is not a matter of natural balance, but _____. New plant defenses unintentionally select for insects with ways to get around them, which in turn help bring about more resilient and resistant plant species. New variations, shading into entire new forms and adaptations, maintain the stalemate.

options.text: a one-sided mechanism benefiting only the insects
a stable ecosystem free from biological conflicts
an ongoing process of reciprocal adaptation
a slow decline in plants' defensive capabilities
a restricted chemical signaling among neighbors

We are now at a point of unprecedented genetic, cultural, and environmental power as a species, and we are linked to nearly every other person on Earth. We are embodied individuals trapped within limited time, but we are also networked data streams, memories, and influencers, and part of a grander humanity. Our decisions today have far-reaching impacts that place a responsibility on us to become good ancestors, to take the long view and time travel forward to imagine the well-being of billions of people whose lives will be lived in the world we are currently making. Centuries ago, leaders of the native North American Iroquois people created "seven generation stewardship," instructing people to consider the impact of every decision on their children, seven generations into the future. question.questionText:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

We are now at a point of unprecedented genetic, cultural, and environmental power as a species, and we are linked to nearly every other person on Earth. We are embodied individuals trapped within limited time, but we are also networked data streams, memories, and influencers, and part of a grander humanity. Our decisions today have far-reaching impacts that place a responsibility on us to become good ancestors, to take the long view and time travel forward to imagine the well-being of billions of people whose lives will be lived in the world we are currently making. Centuries ago, leaders of the native North American Iroquois people created "seven generation stewardship," instructing people to consider the impact of every decision on their children, seven generations into the future. In the precious few decades that Earth is ours, while we enjoy the gardens planted by our ancestors, we must not _____.

options.text: sacrifice our present innovations to honor ancestral traditions
restrict the genetic adaptations necessary for human survival
compromise the rightful prospects of those who will come after us
overlook the cultural achievements woven into our data streams
isolate ourselves from the grander humanity of the Iroquois

keyPoints: 빈칸 문장이 글 전체의 비유적 결론이며, 현재 세대의 장기적 책임과 후손 보호라는 핵심 논지로 수렴됨을 파악하기
비유적 표현(steal the shade from our descendants)이 지니는 함축적 의미를 본문의 'good ancestors', 'future' 관점에서 논리적으로 추상화하기
오답들이 본문의 단어(네트워크, Iroquois 등)를 어떻게 활용하여 논리적 매력도를 높였는지 분석하고 소거하기
structuredData.answerLogic: 원문의 'steal the shade from our descendants(후손들로부터 그늘을 훔치다)'는 후손들이 누려야 할 자원이나 안녕을 현재 세대의 결정으로 훼방하거나 박탈한다는 뜻이므로, 이를 'deprive future generations of their rightful well-being' 계열로 추상화하여 패러프레이즈함.
structuredData.explanation: 이 글은 현재 세대가 지닌 막대한 영향력을 바탕으로 미래 세대를 위해 '좋은 조상'이 되어야 한다는 책임을 강조하고 있습니다. 지문 중간의 Iroquois 사람들의 '7세대 청지기 정신'은 모든 결정이 미래에 미칠 영향을 고려하라는 구체적 사례입니다. 따라서 마지막 문장은 조상들이 심은 정원(유산)을 누리는 동안, 우리는 결코 후손들의 몫(그늘)을 빼앗아서는 안 된다는 결론을 내립니다. 빈칸 위치는 '훔치지 말아야 할 대상' 즉 '미래 세대의 안녕이나 권리를 훼손하는 일'에 해당하므로, '우리 뒤에 올 사람들의 정당한 장래를 위태롭게 하는 것'으로 재진술한 선지가 가장 적절합니다. 오답들은 데이터, Iroquois, 유전 등 본문 어휘를 재활용했으나, 장기적인 책임이라는 글의 핵심에서 벗어나거나 논리적 방향이 잘못되었습니다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

Plants have evolved defenses almost as __(e) diverse__ as the number of genera. Some load their tissues with __(a) harsh__ compounds that either are unpleasant to insects or intoxicate them, encouraging the insects to go bother another plant or at least slowing down their eating. Structural defenses like thick coats of wax on leaves may __(b) prevent__ some insect species from damaging the plant tissues altogether. Nor are individual plants entirely on their own while under attack. Plants have evolved defenses almost as diverse as the number of genera. Some load their tissues with harsh compounds that either are unpleasant to insects or intoxicate them, encouraging the insects to go bother another plant or at least slowing down their eating. Structural defenses like thick coats of wax on leaves may prevent some insect species from damaging the plant tissues altogether. Nor are individual plants entirely on their own while under attack. Plants can release chemical compounds that let their same-species neighbors know that an attack is likely coming, pushing those nearby plants to start building up defensive compounds in their tissues. Some of these cues even attract insect predators, a call for an assist that benefits both the plant and its bug-eating collaborators. The back-and-forth is not a matter of natural balance, but more like a drawn-out evolutionary conversation. New plant defenses (A) [unintentionally / unintentional] select for insects with ways to get around them, (B) [which / what] in turn help bring about more resilient and resistant plant species. New variations, (C) [shading / shaded] into entire new forms and adaptations, maintain the stalemate.

structuredData.explanation: 글쓴이는 글쓰기에서 독자에게 명확성, 관련성, 그리고 적절한 분량을 제공해야 한다고 말하며, 앞 문장에서 너무 많거나 너무 적은 정보를 제공할 경우 독자가 흥미를 잃는다(not clear, who offers too much or too little information)고 경고했습니다. 따라서 글쓴이는 정보를 지나치게(excessively) 많이 주기보다는, 적절하게, 혹은 알맞은 수준으로(appropriately) 제공해야 독자의 관심을 유지할 수 있습니다. 문맥상 과도한 정보 전도를 뜻하는 'excessively'는 어긋나며, 'appropriately'로 고쳐야 올바른 문맥이 됩니다.
structuredData.passageWithMarkers: The basic guidelines for good style are not mysterious; in fact, you use them every day in conversation. In conversation and in writing, we all rely heavily on cooperation to make sense of exchanges, and a __(a) polished__ practical style makes cooperation easier. Writers develop such a style by acknowledging that readers __(b) expect__ the same things that listeners expect in conversation: clarity, relevance, and proportion. If you listen to someone who is not clear, who cannot stay on the topic, or who offers too much or too little information, you will quickly lose interest in the conversation. Writers, too, need to be clear, stay on the topic, and give information __(c) excessively__. In fact, this attention to audience and appropriateness may be even more important in writing than in conversation because writing does not __(d) permit__ the nonverbal communication and immediate feedback that are part of conversation. As writers, we have to __(e) anticipate__ the absent reader's response; in effect, we have to imagine both halves of a virtual conversation.

wrongOptionExplanations.(a): polished(다듬어진, 세련된)는 글을 쓸 때 협력을 원만하게 만들어 주는 실용적 스타일의 긍정적 속성을 나타내므로 문맥상 매우 자연스럽습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(b): expect(기대하다)는 독자와 청자가 소통 방식(명확성, 관련성 등)에서 동등한 기준을 바라고 있음을 뜻하므로 흐름 상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(d): permit(허용하다)는 글쓰기 매체가 비언어적 단서와 즉각적인 피드백을 직접적으로 허용하지 않는다는 속성을 기술하므로 문맥상 맞습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(e): anticipate(예상하다, 예측하다)는 부재 중인 독자의 반응을 미리 그려봐야 하는 필자의 상황을 묘사하므로 논리적으로 정확합니다.
